published_source: Printed Table 4, Panel B (percentage of transactions), column (2) of the published article (papers/mksc/mksc.2022.1356.pdf), read Nov 4 2026; equals the authors' code output to the printed decimals. The spec's column field (5) follows the code's six-column numbering, in which the printed Panel B columns (1)-(3) are columns (4)-(6); the printed location is Panel B, column (2). Earlier: authors' reghdfe line re-run in Stata 16 on the shipped Data products.dta (two-way clustered SE store and skuT, N = 24925 after reghdfe singleton drop); published table value not available (no article text)
replication_status: exact (authors' code output 0.000354068887 (0.000238577203), N 24925, equals printed Table 4, Panel B (percentage of transactions), column (2) 0.0004 (0.0002), N 24,925, to the printed decimals; verified against the article Nov 4 2026)
outcome: share of category transactions involving the SKU (TT_jst/TC_jst)
treatment: label = 1 if the SKU carries at least one front-of-package warning label on that store visit day; first-treatment date = first observed labeled visit day of the store-SKU
notes: Store-SKU-day panel (store visit days, weekdays only), 56 visit days 2016-05-02..2016-07-22, 6 stores visited on 38-48 days each; rows exist only for store-SKU-days with item_qty >= 7 in the shipped file, so the panel is highly unbalanced (median 8 rows per store-SKU). Authors: reghdfe y label if category, absorb(group_store_sku a_week dow) cluster(store skuT) (docx code lines 12/26/40 for Tables 2-4, 64 for Table 6). fixest feols(y ~ label | group_store_sku + a_week + dow, cluster = ~store + skuT) reproduces the Stata re-run to 9 digits (SE to 6). No article text in the project: published table values not checked; published_coef is the authors' code re-run on the shipped data; table numbering (Tables 2/3/4 = cereals/chocolates/cookies, Table 6 columns in that order) is inferred from code comments. PIPELINE DEVIATIONS: (1) label is non-absorbing; run_spec drops post-adoption rows with label = 0 (Hull fn 6). (2) Calendar time = visit date, so run_spec's TWFE uses date FE, which nest the authors' additive week-of-year + day-of-week FE (each date maps to one week x dow cell). (3) Single cluster variable skuT instead of two-way store x skuT (only 6 stores). (4) run_spec keeps singletons (reghdfe drops them); coefficients unaffected. 1,665 store-SKUs: 534 never labeled, 613 switchers (53 distinct first-label dates; 262 switch off), 518 labeled at first observation (184 switch off; 155 on the first sample day); 2689 post-adoption label = 0 rows dropped by run_spec. Authors' FE (week + dow) on the post-drop sample: 0.000282; date FE on the post-drop sample: 0.000311 (raw units).
